stances.claim: The SC correctly read the Constitution: LGUs' 40% share should be based on all 'national taxes,' not just NIRC taxes, and must be automatically released.
The prospective (not retroactive) implementation was the right call -- Dominguez's P1.5 trillion retroactivity concern is thus allayed.
The SC decision provides a 'refreshing pause' for federalism proponents to restudy the economic costs -- Diokno, Villegas, Abola, and Manasan's candid warnings cannot be cavalierly ignored.
stances.rhetorical_move: reframing an SC ruling as a policy pause signal

stances.claim: Federalism proponents need to unify and simplify their proposals -- three divergent drafts (ConCom, PDP-Laban, House committee) with confusing voices explain why opinion polls show very little support.
Sen. Lacson's argument that implementing the LGC is sufficient to achieve devolution's grand goal without revising the Constitution deserves serious consideration.
stances.rhetorical_move: endorsement of the simpler, law-respecting alternative

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban reports on the Supreme Court's 10-3 ruling (July 10, 2018, per J. Bersamin) that LGUs are entitled to 40% of all national taxes -- not just national internal revenue taxes under the Local Government Code of 1991 -- plus automatic release, pursuant to Article X, Section 6. Per his confidential sources, the Court decided on prospective (not retroactive) implementation, thus allaying Finance Secretary Dominguez's concern that a retroactive computation from 1992 could reach a staggering P1.5 trillion. Budget Secretary Diokno still warned of a potential 6% deficit and credit-rating downgrade threatening the 'Build, build, build' program; NEDA Secretary Pernia connected fiscal devolution to federalism's economic risks. Presidential spokesperson Roque allayed Pernia but did not address Diokno's concerns. Economists Villegas and Abola of the University of Asia and the Pacific warned that federalism is expensive, unnecessary, and potentially hyperinflationary (1,000% consumer price surges in some Latin American and European federal states); PIDS researcher Manasan estimated P55 billion in annual additional costs. Sen. Lacson tweeted that simply implementing the LGC could achieve devolution without revising the Constitution. The column closes with two prescriptions: the SC ruling is a 'refreshing pause' for proponents to restudy costs, and the proponents urgently need to unify three divergent and confusing drafts (ConCom, PDP-Laban, House committee) whose incoherence explains why opinion polls show very little support for federalism.
